## PROVEN NECESSARY: with the `search_files` lie fixed, e369's close STILL exhausts — a different loop formed

Third exhaustion of the e369 completion verification, and this one rules out the cause we just fixed.

**The `search_files` fix ([rebar:bf31-fd55-d28d-4b7a], Gerrit 1433, merged as `85805e02f1`) is live and
working in the exact interpreter that ran the close** — verified directly, not assumed:

    module file: /Users/joeoakhart/agent-5200-diag/src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py
    fix present in LOADED module: True
    search_files('os.path.isfile', 'src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py')
      -> 'src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py:138: if os.path.isfile(base):'

That is the call shape which previously returned `(no matches)`. The measured loop's fuel is gone.

**And the close still died the same way**, at the DEFAULT budget (480) — deliberately not raised,
because bf31's trace established ~118 genuinely distinct calls are needed, so 480 is ~3.5x adequate
and raising it treats a loop as a capacity problem:

    step 'decide@then/verify' failed: agent exceeded its step budget (max_iterations=480)

**Conclusion: the `search_files` lie was necessary but NOT sufficient.** A different unproductive cycle
forms, and with no loop breaker on the primary verify step the run is killed EMPTY rather than landing
a verdict. That is exactly what this ticket exists to fix, and it is now evidenced rather than
predicted.

### Why this ticket is now the blocking one

bf31's fix shape listed this as item (2) — `RunRequest.tool_step_limit` is a shipped primitive
(`llm/agent_call.py:64-75`) that is never set for the primary verify step
(`llm/workflow/runs.py:327-338`); its only caller is bounded recovery. The distinction that matters:
a step limit makes the run **land with a verdict** instead of being killed with nothing. Every other
remedy currently available produces no verdict at all, and the only documented exit from that state is
`--force-close` — the unattested close this project forbids.

Three exhaustions now (480, 1600, and 480-with-the-tool-fixed) say the gate cannot verify this epic
without a structural breaker, independent of any single tool bug.

**Not fixed here and not forced.** e369 remains `in_progress` with all 59 descendants closed and
certified, 14/14 criteria met, and its harness green on `main` (run 30986591446). Only the status bit
is unset, and it stays unset until a genuine verdict exists.

# RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1) — MEASURED: the post-bf31 run is NOT a loop. It is genuine breadth against a FLAT budget, and there is no forced landing.

Fourth exhaustion, reproduced under my own instrumentation on `origin/main` @ `85805e02f1`
(the commit that carries bf31's `search_files` fix). Every claim below is measured, not inferred.

## 1. This ticket's own framing is REFUTED: no new cycle forms

The comment above predicted "a DIFFERENT unproductive cycle now forms". It does not.
I re-ran `verify_completion(e369, graph=False, source="attested", ref="HEAD")` with every agent
tool call logged (trace: `/tmp/c827-trace.jsonl`, 258 rows) and compared it to bf31's pre-fix trace
(`/tmp/bf31-trace-evidence.jsonl`, 264 rows):

| | bf31 run (pre-fix) | THIS run (post-fix) |
|---|---|---|
| tool calls to death | 264 | **258** |
| distinct call signatures | 135 (51%) | **238 (92%)** |
| novelty, first block | 94-98% | 100% |
| novelty, **final** block | **0%** (calls 199-264) | **93.8% / 100%** |
| longest repeated signature | **x37** | **x6** |
| "next 20 calls all repeats" | call #121 | **never** |
| wall clock | 1074s | 1043s |

**bf31's fix worked.** The closed 4-call cycle is gone; novelty stays 72-100% through the *last*
block. The verifier is doing genuine, non-repetitive evidence gathering (201 `search_files`, 46
`read_file`, 6 `list_directory`, 5 `show_ticket`) and simply runs out of TURNS.

That is exactly the position [rebar:a89d-4dd2-f421-417a] argued from its own instrumentation
(`requests=240 tool_calls=475 distinct=451 max_consecutive_repeat=1` — "It is NOT a runaway loop").
a89d is **confirmed for the post-bf31 world** and should be read as live, not superseded.

**The defect statement is unchanged by this, and that is the point** (see §3): under *either*
frame — loop or breadth — the run is killed at the exact moment a tool-free turn would have
produced a verdict.

## 2. PROVEN ROOT CAUSE

**The primary completion-verify agent step is dispatched with no forced-landing boundary, so
budget exhaustion kills the run instead of landing it.**

The causal chain, each link cited and each dynamically confirmed:

1. `build_agent_request` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py:327-339`) constructs the `RunRequest`
   for every workflow agent step and **never sets `tool_step_limit`**; the v3 step schema is
   closed, so `completion-verification.yaml`'s `decide@then/verify` step has no way to supply one.
2. The shipped forced-landing primitive is therefore dormant for the one step that needs it:
   `agent_call.py:64-73` (`if req.tool_step_limit is not None and tools:` -> toolsets rewritten to
   `.filtered(lambda ctx,_: ctx.run_step <= limit)`). Its ONLY production setter is the bounded
   recovery sub-call (`completion_recovery.py:471`, `_EVIDENCE_TOOL_STEPS=16`). Current behaviour is
   pinned by a test: `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_token_recovery.py:132`
   `assert runner.requests[-1].tool_step_limit is None`.
3. The budget is FLAT: `build_usage_limits` (`structured_run.py:399-412`) sets
   `request_limit = max(1, ceil(eff_max_iter/2))` = **240** at the default `max_iterations=480`,
   and `tool_calls_limit = max(8, eff_max_iter)` = 480. Neither scales with ticket size or
   criteria count.
4. Exceeding it raises pydantic-ai `UsageLimitExceeded`; `interpret_failure`
   (`structured_run.py:75-101`) computes a repetition diagnostic, attaches it to
   `budget_err.diagnostic`, and raises **`LLMRunnerError`**.
5. `CompletionAgentStep.run` (`completion_recovery.py:429-432`) catches ONLY
   `UnretryableOutputError` and only when `_is_token_exhaustion` holds. Per `errors.py:29-46`,
   `LLMRunnerError` is a strict **ancestor** of `StructuredOutputError` -> `UnretryableOutputError`,
   so the clause can never match.
6. `failure_diagnostic` stays `None`, so `raise_completion_workflow_failure`
   (`completion_recovery.py:378-402`) skips `emit_gate_error` and raises a bare `LLMError` at
   `:400` — no verdict, no `gate_error_v1` sidecar, diagnostic discarded one frame from the surface.

### Discriminating experiments (deterministic, `FunctionModel` + `model_override`, seconds not minutes)

**E1 — does withdrawing tools actually force a landing under the pydantic-ai structured stack?**
A model that unconditionally calls a tool whenever any tool is offered; `mode="structured"`,
`output_schema="completion_verdict"`:

* **Arm A** (`tool_step_limit=None` — the production shape): `LLMRunnerError: agent exceeded its
  step budget`, 20 requests / 20 tool calls, diagnostic `tool_calls_distinct: 1,
  max_consecutive_repeat: 20`. **NO verdict.**
* **Arm B** (`tool_step_limit=6`): `tools_offered` per request `[6,6,6,6,6,6,0]` ->
  **a valid `completion_verdict` returned** (`verdict=FAIL`, 1 finding) in 7 requests.

This kills the objection recorded on [rebar:9a08-614d-a9d4-4a81], whose prototype withdrew tools at
`run_step > 16` and found "the exhausted agent emitted unparseable prose". Under
`mode="structured"` the Agent is constructed with `output_type` (`structured_run.py:191-196`), so
the landing turn is schema-constrained. The half 9a08 discarded now works.

**E2 — end-to-end through the REAL gate.** The same looping model injected via
`verify_completion(ticket, graph=False, runner=PydanticAIRunner(cfg, model_override=...))`
reproduced the production surface EXACTLY: `LLMError: completion verification workflow did not
produce a verdict: step 'decide@then/verify' failed: agent exceeded its step budget
(max_iterations=480 …)`, with **`diagnostic = null`**, **`emit_gate_error` called 0 times**, 240
model requests. Links 4-6 confirmed at runtime, not by reading source.

**E3 — the live 258-call run** (§1) confirms link 3 against the real model: death at the request
ceiling with 92% distinct signatures.

## 3. The size dependence — measured, and it is NOT descendant count

The operator's question ("why do 19-descendant epics close and this 59-descendant one not?").
Measured across all 205 epics in the store:

* **Descendant count does NOT drive the verifier's context.** The close gate passes `graph=False`,
  so `assemble_context` inlines the ticket's OWN description + comments and nothing else
  (`gate_ops.py`, `operations.assemble_context`). Counter-example: `6001` has **39 descendants** and
  a **2,194-char** context. The 59 descendants enter only as ~88s of deterministic pre-LLM CPU
  (`child_closure_findings` + `epic_bug_floor_findings`), never as tool calls — consistent with
  bf31's "only 5 `show_ticket` calls".
* **`assemble_context` has NO cap and NO truncation** on the primary path. The
  `_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS = 100_000` at `completion_recovery.py:65` is a **recovery precondition that
  REFUSES** (`:169` raises `CompletionRecoveryError`), not a truncator, and it is not on the primary
  path at all. **The "context is silently truncated, so the verifier hunts for what was dropped"
  chain is REFUTED** — nothing is dropped. (e369 sits at 99,347 vs that 100,000 refusal bound —
  653 chars of headroom — which matters for [rebar:fd84-92b4-01ba-4911], not for this failure.)
* **Context size at signature time, for every epic that carries a `completion-verifier` signature:**

  | epic | gate signature | signed | criteria | context @ sign |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 5fd2 | completion-verifier: PASS | 2026-06-24 | n/a | **169,463** |
  | e0e2 | completion-verifier: PASS | 2026-06-25 | 9 | **131,519** |
  | e68d | completion-verifier: PASS | 2026-07-12 | 15 | 19,568 |
  | 86ac | completion-verifier: PASS | 2026-07-19 | 10 | 10,056 |
  | a492 | completion-verifier: PASS | 2026-07-30 | 3 | 2,031 |
  | 2f4c | completion-verifier: PASS | 2026-08-04 | 9 | 3,718 |
  | **e369** | **plan-review only** | — | **14** | **95,139** |

  **Context size alone does not predict failure** — 5fd2 (169k) and e0e2 (131k) passed this gate.
  But both were **June**. Since 2026-07-01 the largest context to pass is **19,568** (e68d), and
  e369 at 95,139 is **~5x** that. I record this as a strong correlation over a 5-run post-June
  sample, **not** a proven mechanism; I did not establish what changed between late June and July.
* **The honest size statement:** the budget is FLAT (240 requests, independent of ticket size or
  criteria count) while the evidence-gathering workload scales with the ticket's volume of
  code-grounded verifiable claims. e369's 14 criteria span two adapter trees with per-symbol and
  per-import assertions; the trace shows that costing 258 genuine tool calls. Smaller epics finish
  inside the flat budget; e369 does not. This is the same gap `99e22e4c23` (ticket
  [rebar:d59e-e042-2b94-4b70]) already named as follow-up work: *"its live blocker is the primary
  verifier's flat step budget, which does not scale with criteria count."*
* **Larger epics DID historically bypass this gate — confirmed.** `1d96` (21 descendants) and
  `bf50` (19 descendants) each carry an explicit audit comment: *"FORCE_CLOSE: close gate(s)
  bypassed by user approval — no completion/signature attestation was signed."* **20 of 205 epics
  carry a FORCE_CLOSE audit comment.** So "the gate has never verified an epic this large" is not
  luck — the historical exit for large epics has been the unattested one this project forbids.

## 4. History — this class was worked SIX times, never at the loop-breaking layer

* [rebar:c7c5-12ea-ad68-4690] (the epic that CREATED the verifier) was itself **force-closed**, with
  *"a monolithic whole-epic LLM verification exceeds the practical step budget (a documented
  limitation)"*. The gate shipped with this as an accepted limitation on day one.
* [rebar:7c58-5b15-f302-49db] listed *"Stronger budget steering (hard tool-call cap)"* as a
  candidate and **explicitly deferred it**.
* [rebar:b2bb-2ac7-5ce3-4412]'s plan review advised *"a per-op floor for the agentic verifier
  instead of raising the GLOBAL default"* — **explicitly rejected as out of scope**.
* Budget ceilings were raised **five times** instead (`c48162ca6b` 25->50, `50490e20a3`
  `_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS` 240->480 — self-described *"interim, blind-ish bump"*, `98011a3f29` 50->250).
* [rebar:9a08-614d-a9d4-4a81] (`dcc90ced45`, Gerrit 985) **built `tool_step_limit`** — comment
  verbatim: *"Remove all tools after this pydantic-ai run step, leaving a final turn that can
  summarize gathered evidence as text… Executable convergence boundary."* It was built for the
  recovery sub-calls only. **No commit anywhere considers and rejects applying it to the primary
  verify step — it was never wired, not deliberately excluded.**
* [rebar:a89d-4dd2-f421-417a] (`5f00bf5253`) built the repetition DIAGNOSTIC, explicitly
  report-only: *"The question 'is this a runaway or a big job?' was therefore unanswerable."*
  Nothing consumes `max_consecutive_repeat` to intervene.
* [rebar:59bc-b9ba-021a-435f] (`964791dd8f`) shipped a budget-exhaustion **recovery for
  plan-review** — a verify step that exhausts producing an outcome rather than an exception. Direct
  structural precedent, **scoped to plan-review only**; the completion path has no equivalent.

**Detector built, remedy not wired — confirmed, and it is not a regression.** The detector (a89d)
and the breaker (9a08) were built ~3 days apart for different purposes and never joined. The
`docs/llm-framework.md:707-712` wording (*"a high recursion limit means you're paying for a loop,
fix the loop"*) traces to `76af85ba19` (2026-06-18), which shipped `RunRequest.output_strategy=
"extract"` — a genuine tool-LESS structured-extraction landing — and live-validated it. That
mechanism was **deleted** in the LangChain->pydantic-ai cutover (`2e9bd4205f`, 2026-06-22) and the
doc was rewritten (`88ac13a210`) to assert `mode="structured"` inherits the property — *"the finding
carries over to the pydantic-ai runtime"*, an assertion, not a re-measurement. Note for the record:
5fd2 and e0e2 passed on 06-24/06-25, i.e. **after** that removal, so the removal alone does not
explain the current failure; I am NOT claiming a clean regression there.

## 5. Legitimacy: `incomplete-implementation` (unlocks a repair)

The capability was designed, built, tested and given one consumer; the primary consumer was never
wired. Cited authority:
* `agent_call.py:64-73` + `tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py:90-144` — the mechanism ships with
  tests.
* `docs/llm-framework.md:707-712` — the project's stated invariant that a step budget is not the
  lever.
* `99e22e4c23` ([rebar:d59e-e042-2b94-4b70]) names the gap as follow-up work in-tree.
* The operator-facing message the code emits — *"Raise REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS or narrow the task"*
  (`structured_run.py:95-99`) — advises machinery that sits one `except` clause away and is
  unreachable.

## 6. Fix shape (NOT yet implemented — this ticket is unclaimed)

**Site: (a) set `tool_step_limit` on the primary verify step.** Rejected alternatives:
* **(b) make bounded recovery reachable for `LLMRunnerError`** ([rebar:fd84-92b4-01ba-4911]) —
  engages only *after* 240 requests are burned, then re-pays N criteria x 40 iterations; e369 sits
  653 chars under its `_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS` refusal bound; and a89d records its
  `_EVIDENCE_OUTPUT_TOKENS=4096` clamp truncating evidence into **false-negative FAILs**. Larger
  behavioural change, known false-FAIL record. Leave to fd84.
* **(c) a runner-level default** — widest blast radius on a runtime every gate shares, and it
  collides with `runner.py:531`, which uses `req.tool_step_limit is not None` as a proxy for "this
  is a bounded-evidence *text* call".

**Seam:** a `with:` input on the YAML step, threaded through `build_agent_request`. This is the
established extension point, stated inline at `runs.py:165-166`: *"Carried as a `with:` input (not
a step field) because the v3 step schema is closed/immutable"* — precedent `step_budget_per_item`,
`output_tokens_per_item`, `output_budget: model_max` (a **sentinel, not a number** — the shape AC#3
wants), `temperature`. Note this would be the first such knob that must reach `RunRequest` rather
than `cfg`.

**Derivation (AC#3), single-sourced off `structured_run.py:407`:**

    tool_step_limit = max(0, req_limit - LANDING_RESERVE)     # LANDING_RESERVE = 1

-> 239 at `max_iterations=480`, 24 at 50, 3 at 8, 0 at 2. Measured: `run_step` allows requests
`1..limit` and the landing is request `limit+1`, so `limit <= req_limit - 1`. Do **not** subtract
`OUTPUT_RETRIES`: the PROMPTED retry loop calls `agent.run_sync` afresh per attempt
(`structured_run.py:214-216`) and each attempt gets a fresh `run_step` and a fresh request budget
(measured: attempt 2 starts at request 8 of a 10-request budget). Use `max(0, …)` not `max(1, …)`:
at `eff_max_iter=2`, `limit=0` lands in one tool-free turn whereas `limit=1` would still exhaust.

**AC#4 (no change to a converging run) — measured.** A run converging in 3 requests is byte-identical
at `tool_step_limit` `None` / 100 / 238: 3 requests, `tools_offered=[6,6,6]`, same `PASS`. The
predicate at `agent_call.py:71` is unconditionally true below the limit and the tool *surface* is
preserved by the `FunctionToolset(tools)` rewrite.

### The one thing a plan here MUST NOT miss

`tool_step_limit` gates **model requests** (`run_ctx.run_step`). `build_usage_limits` installs a
**second, independent** kill path — `tool_calls_limit = max(8, eff_max_iter)` = 2x `request_limit` —
which a `run_step`-keyed predicate does not bound at all. Measured sweep at
`max_iterations=480` (`request_limit=240`, `tool_calls_limit=480`):

| tool calls / request | `tool_step_limit` | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 239 | OK — verdict returned (478/480 calls) |
| **3** | 239 | **`LLMRunnerError`** — 483/480 |
| 3 | 216 (0.9x) | **`LLMRunnerError`** |
| 3 | 180 (0.75x) | **`LLMRunnerError`** |
| 6 | 120 (0.5x) | **`LLMRunnerError`** |

**No fraction of `request_limit` guarantees the landing**, because per-request tool-call fan-out is
unbounded. My live run sat at 258 calls / 240 requests = **1.075**, comfortably clear; a89d measured
a real run at **475/240 = 1.979**, clearing the 480 ceiling by **2 calls**. The remedy is available
and cheap: `run_ctx.usage.tool_calls` is live and exact inside the predicate (measured
`(run_step, tool_calls) = [(1,0), (2,3), (3,6)]`), so the fix is a two-term predicate at
`agent_call.py:70-71`, not a new mechanism. A fix that sets only `tool_step_limit` will pass a
1-call-per-request test and can still die in production.

**Residual risk to weigh in review:** a forced landing yields a verdict on incomplete evidence, and
`completion_verdict` has **no INDETERMINATE** — `_norm_verdict` normalizes anything but `"PASS"` to
`"FAIL"` (`contracts.py`; re-applied at `completion.py:358-395`). So it **fails closed** (blocks a
close, never certifies), and under-evidenced FAIL is already the prompt's sanctioned behaviour:
`reviewers/completion_verifier.md:150-151` — *"If, after a bounded search, you cannot find evidence
that a requirement is met, record what you searched and treat it as NOT MET — never assume."* The
genuine risk is a *quiet* false FAIL, indistinguishable from a considered one; the landing turn
should say so in `detail`.

## 7. Can e369 close honestly once this lands?

**It becomes possible for the first time, but it is not guaranteed and this fix does not promise a
PASS.** The fix converts "killed with no verdict, `--force-close` the only exit" into "a real
`completion_verdict` on ~239 requests of genuine evidence". Two things could still make that verdict
a FAIL, neither in this ticket's scope:
1. e369's criterion #1 — *"every child story is closed and its change is `Verified +1` on Gerrit"* —
   has **no evidence any repository tool can reach**; the deterministic child-closure proof the
   precheck already computes (`blocking=0, uncertified=0`) is collapsed to a boolean at
   `gate_ops.py:132` and never reaches the verifier's prompt (`completion-verification.yaml:48-56`
   wires only `context`). This is the most likely route to a genuine FAIL.
2. The flat budget still does not scale with criteria count ([rebar:a89d-4dd2-f421-417a],
   [rebar:d59e-e042-2b94-4b70]), so a forced landing on a ticket this size lands on *partial*
   evidence by construction.

**e369 remains `in_progress` and untouched.** Nothing was force-closed and no status was changed.

Evidence: `/tmp/c827-trace.jsonl` (258 rows, this run), `/tmp/c827-run.log`,
`/tmp/bf31-trace-evidence.jsonl` (264 rows, bf31's pre-fix run) for the side-by-side.

# RE-SCOPED against the limit's stated PURPOSE — and the flat forced landing is now WITHDRAWN

Design intent supplied by the operator: **the step budget exists to bound FAILURES (observed runaway
tool calls under error conditions), NOT to cap capacity. It was explicitly never meant to restrict
tool calls for large epics.** That inverts my previous plan, which proposed a flat forced landing at
~239 requests. I ran three more live gate runs to test the alternatives against that intent.

## Four REAL runs of this gate, same codebase state (except bf31's, which predates its own fix)

| run | criteria | calls | **distinct** | redundant | distinct ratio | outcome | `w24 distinct<=0.5` fires |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FULL | 14 | 258 | **238** | 20 | **0.922** | died empty | **never** |
| SPLIT-A | 7 | 257 | **76** | **181** | 0.296 | died empty | **call 88** |
| SPLIT-B | 7 | 270 | 167 | 103 | 0.619 | died empty | **call 196** |
| bf31 pre-fix | 14 | 264 | 135 | 129 | 0.511 | died empty | **call 151** |

**THREE OF FOUR RUNS LOOPED.** Only the full post-bf31 run was clean. Repetition wasted **40-70% of
every pathological run** (181, 103 and 129 redundant calls). SPLIT-A's loop is textbook: the
IDENTICAL call `search_files("_loader", "src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler")` repeated **144 times**,
returning the identical 12,554-char result each time, from call #81 to the end. SPLIT-B looped 62x on
`search_files("deleted", tests/.../test_backend_characterization.py)` -> an **honest** `(no matches)`
that the agent simply would not accept.

So the runaway-under-error-conditions failure the budget was built to bound is **the dominant,
reproducible failure of this gate today, and it is currently unbounded**. That is the thing to fix.

## WITHDRAWN: the flat forced landing at ~239 requests

It contradicts the stated intent and the data refutes its necessity. The ONLY run that was genuinely
budget-bound by *breadth* is the clean FULL run — 92% distinct, 93.8-100% novelty in its final block.
Cutting that off at 239 requests would land a verdict on deliberately-truncated evidence for
legitimate work: a worse verdict, not a safer one. Dropped.

## PRIMARY FIX: wire an actuator to a repetition discriminator that actually works

### The existing detector's headline metric is BROKEN — measured, filed as [rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0]

`max_consecutive_repeat` (`src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:213-235`) counts only *adjacent identical*
signatures, so it is blind to any cycle of length >= 2:

| trace | what it is | `max_consecutive_repeat` |
|---|---|---|
| bf31 pre-fix | a genuine **4-call cycle** repeated 31-37x | **1** |
| FULL (healthy) | genuine breadth | **5** |

The pathological run scores **below** the healthy one. This is precisely why
[rebar:a89d-4dd2-f421-417a] measured `max_consecutive_repeat=1` and concluded *"It is NOT a runaway
loop"*. **An actuator wired to this metric would fire on healthy work and miss real cycles.** It
catches SPLIT-A's 1-cycle (137) only because that degenerate case is the one shape it can see.

### The discriminator that does work: a windowed distinct-ratio

Lowest distinct-ratio over any trailing window, across all four runs:

| window | bf31 | SPLIT-A | SPLIT-B | **FULL (healthy)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 0.250 | **0.062** | 0.062 | **0.750** |
| 24 | 0.167 | **0.042** | — | **0.833** |
| 32 | 0.125 | **0.031** | — | **0.875** |

A rule `distinct(last 24 tool calls) <= 0.50` fires on **all three** pathological runs (calls 151, 88,
196) and **never** on the healthy one, with a ~5x margin. It is also **order-insensitive** (a set
cardinality over a window), so unlike adjacency it is robust to tool calls completing out of emission
order — which matters, because these traces log completion order.

### Feasibility — confirmed, and it needs no new detector

* `run_ctx.messages` **is** available inside the tool-filter predicate (verified against
  `pydantic_ai.tools.RunContext` fields), alongside `run_ctx.usage.tool_calls`.
* `usage_log.failure_usage` duck-types on a plain message list (`type(m).__name__ == "ModelResponse"`,
  `"ToolCallPart"`), so **a89d's signature logic runs verbatim on the live history** — the remedy is
  literally wiring the existing detector to act, once [rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0] gives it a signal
  that separates cycles from breadth.
* The actuator is the **already-shipped** mechanism: withdraw tools (`agent_call.py:64-73`) so the
  agent must land a verdict on the evidence it has, instead of being killed with nothing.

### The `tool_calls_limit` path is still covered — as a FAILURE bound, not a workload ceiling

`build_usage_limits` (`structured_run.py:399-412`) installs a second, independent kill path:
`tool_calls_limit = max(8, eff_max_iter)` = 480 vs `request_limit` 240. `run_step` does not bound it.
Measured: at 3 tool calls/request a `tool_step_limit` of 239, 216 **and** 180 all still die; my clean
run sat at 258/240 = 1.075 and a89d measured a real run at 475/240 = **1.979** — clearing 480 by 2
calls. Because the discriminator is computed over **tool calls**, a runaway that burns calls without
burning requests trips it on the same signal. No separate workload ceiling is introduced.
(Enforcement point established from the vendored source: `UsageLimits.check_before_tool_call`,
`pydantic_ai/usage.py:412-419`, called at `_agent_graph.py:1703-1706` with **projected** usage — it
raises *before* executing, so the guard must act while headroom remains.)

## The AC-split fallback — TESTED LIVE, and it is NOT sufficient

Split BY EXPLICIT AC INDEX (never inferred), each half carrying the **full** context: 14 criteria ->
7 + 7, context 99,347 -> 96,631 (A) / 96,086 (B) chars. The criteria set **does** partition cleanly —
each is an independent `- [x]` item, so this is mechanically sound.

**Both halves still died empty.** And the workload benefit is unproven:

| run | criteria | distinct calls | **distinct per criterion** |
|---|---|---|---|
| FULL | 14 | 238 | 17.0 |
| SPLIT-A | 7 | 76 | 10.9 |
| SPLIT-B | 7 | 167 | **23.9** |

SPLIT-B spent **more** evidence per criterion than the full run. Per-criterion cost varies 10.9-23.9
across runs, so run-to-run variance dominates any halving effect — on this evidence the split does not
reliably bring a run inside the budget. Verdict combination (FAIL in either half => FAIL overall) is
straightforward, but two signatures over two disjoint criteria subsets is a **material change to what
the attestation means** and needs its own design. **The split is a capability, not this bug's fix.**
It should be its own ticket if wanted — and note it is only viable at all *with* the repetition
actuator, since both halves were killed by loops, not by breadth.

## Honest statement of what this fix delivers

**It does NOT make e369's full-criteria close reach a verdict.** The clean FULL run never trips the
discriminator, so it would still die budget-exhausted on genuine breadth — and per the stated intent
that is the correct outcome, not a bug to paper over. What the fix does deliver:

* the three pathological runs above would have been cut at calls 88 / 151 / 196 and **landed a
  verdict** on the evidence gathered, instead of being killed empty with `--force-close` as the only
  exit;
* 40-70% of each pathological run's spend is reclaimed;
* the failure mode the budget was introduced for is bounded for the first time.

A path to e369 reaching a verdict exists — **AC split PLUS the actuator** (each half's genuine work,
76 and 167 distinct calls, sits inside the budget once its loop is cut) — but that is two tickets, and
neither promises a **PASS**. Criterion #1's Gerrit half remains unreachable by any repo tool
([rebar:6ec8-24c7-182b-40d0]), and the flat budget still does not scale with claim volume
([rebar:a89d-4dd2-f421-417a], [rebar:d59e-e042-2b94-4b70]).

## Dependency

This ticket's actuator needs a discriminator that separates cycles from breadth, so it is **blocked on
[rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0]** (the `max_consecutive_repeat` blind spot). Wiring an actuator to
today's metric would fire on healthy runs and miss real cycles — the exact inversion measured above.

Evidence: `/tmp/c827-trace.jsonl` (FULL, 258), `/tmp/c827-split-A.jsonl` (257),
`/tmp/c827-split-B.jsonl` (270), `/tmp/bf31-trace-evidence.jsonl` (264), and the run logs beside them.

compiled_state.description:
# The completion verifier cannot bound a runaway: repetition is detected but nothing acts on it

## The defect

The completion-verify agent step has **no bound on a runaway**. When the agent falls into a
repeating tool-call cycle it burns its entire step budget on redundant calls and is then **killed
with no verdict at all** — leaving `--force-close`, the unattested close this project forbids, as
the only exit. **20 of 205 epics in this store already carry a `FORCE_CLOSE` audit comment**,
including `1d96` (21 descendants) and `bf50` (19), so this is the established escape hatch, not a
hypothetical.

The step budget exists to bound exactly this failure. It does not: it is a flat ceiling that stops
the run *after* the waste, rather than a guard that detects the runaway and makes the agent land.

### Measured: three of four real runs of this gate LOOP

Four instrumented live runs, same codebase state except bf31's which predates its own fix:

| run | criteria | calls | **distinct** | redundant | distinct ratio | outcome | `w24 distinct<=0.5` fires |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FULL | 14 | 258 | **238** | 20 | **0.922** | died empty | **never** |
| SPLIT-A | 7 | 257 | **76** | **181** | 0.296 | died empty | **call 88** |
| SPLIT-B | 7 | 270 | 167 | 103 | 0.619 | died empty | **call 196** |
| bf31 pre-fix | 14 | 264 | 135 | 129 | 0.511 | died empty | **call 151** |

Repetition wasted **40-70% of every pathological run**. SPLIT-A is textbook: the IDENTICAL call
`search_files("_loader", "src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler")` repeated **144 times**, returning the
identical 12,554-char result each time, from call #81 to the end. SPLIT-B looped 62x on
`search_files("deleted", tests/.../test_backend_characterization.py)` -> an **honest** `(no matches)`
the agent simply would not accept. Only the clean FULL run was genuine breadth.

### The mechanism that turns a runaway into "no verdict"

1. `build_agent_request` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py:327-339`) builds the `RunRequest` for every
   workflow agent step and never sets `tool_step_limit`; the v3 step schema is closed, so
   `completion-verification.yaml`'s `decide@then/verify` step has no way to supply one.
2. The shipped forced-landing primitive is therefore dormant for the one step that needs it:
   `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py:64-73` rewrites the toolsets to
   `.filtered(lambda ctx, _: ctx.run_step <= limit)`. Its only production setter is the bounded
   recovery sub-call (`completion_recovery.py:471`, `_EVIDENCE_TOOL_STEPS=16`).
3. Exhaustion raises pydantic-ai `UsageLimitExceeded` -> `interpret_failure`
   (`structured_run.py:75-101`) raises `LLMRunnerError` -> `CompletionAgentStep.run`
   (`completion_recovery.py:429-432`) catches only `UnretryableOutputError`, of which
   `LLMRunnerError` is a strict **ancestor** (`errors.py:29-46`) -> `failure_diagnostic` stays
   `None` -> `raise_completion_workflow_failure` raises a bare `LLMError` at
   `completion_recovery.py:400`. No verdict, no `gate_error_v1` sidecar, computed diagnostic
   discarded one frame from the surface.

---

## WITHDRAWN PLAN (kept visible deliberately — the wrong version is the instructive artifact)

> **An earlier revision of this ticket proposed a FLAT FORCED LANDING: set
> `tool_step_limit = max(0, request_limit - 1)` (= 239 at the default budget) unconditionally on the
> primary verify step, so tools are withdrawn near the end of the budget and the agent must emit a
> verdict.**
>
> **WHY IT WAS WITHDRAWN.** The design intent of the step budget is to bound **FAILURES** — runaway
> tool calls under error conditions — and **NOT to cap capacity**; it was explicitly never meant to
> restrict tool calls for large epics. A flat landing inverts that: it caps capacity for every run,
> including healthy ones.
>
> The data refutes its necessity as well as its intent. The only run that was genuinely budget-bound
> by *breadth* is the clean FULL run — 92% distinct signatures, 93.8-100% novelty in its final block.
> Truncating that at 239 requests would land a verdict on deliberately-truncated evidence for
> legitimate work: **a worse verdict, not a safer one**, and on a gate that SIGNS its output.
>
> The withdrawn plan was not wrong about the mechanism — links 1-3 above still hold, and the
> ACTUATOR it named (withdraw tools so the agent lands) is retained. It was wrong about the
> **trigger**: budget-proximity instead of runaway-detection.

---

## THE FIX: trigger the existing actuator on repetition, not on budget proximity

Withdraw tools **when a runaway is detected**, so the agent lands a verdict on the evidence it has.
Healthy breadth is never touched.

### Blocker: the existing detector's headline metric is INVERTED on real data

`max_consecutive_repeat` (`src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:213-235`) counts only *adjacent identical*
signatures, so it is blind to any cycle of length >= 2:

| trace | what it is | **`max_consecutive_repeat`** |
|---|---|---|
| bf31 pre-fix | a genuine **4-call cycle** repeated 31-37x | **1** |
| FULL | **healthy** breadth | **5** |

**The pathological run scores 1; the healthy run scores 5.** An actuator wired to this metric would
fire on healthy work and miss real cycles — the exact inversion of what is wanted. It catches
SPLIT-A's 144x 1-cycle (137) only because the degenerate 1-cycle is the single shape it can see.
This is also why ticket a89d-4dd2-f421-417a measured `max_consecutive_repeat=1` and concluded *"It
is NOT a runaway loop."*

**This ticket therefore `depends_on` [rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0]**, which fixes the metric. Building
the actuator against today's signal is the one thing this evidence forbids. Sequencing is not
optional here.

### The discriminator that works: a windowed distinct-ratio

Lowest distinct-ratio over any trailing window, all four runs:

| window | bf31 | SPLIT-A | SPLIT-B | **FULL (healthy)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 0.250 | **0.062** | 0.062 | **0.750** |
| 24 | 0.167 | **0.042** | — | **0.833** |
| 32 | 0.125 | **0.031** | — | **0.875** |

`distinct(last 24 tool calls) <= 0.50` fires on **all three** pathological runs (calls 151, 88, 196)
and **never** on the healthy one — a ~5x margin. It is a set cardinality over a window, therefore
**order-insensitive**, so unlike adjacency its value does not change when tool calls complete out of emission
order (which these traces do).

### Feasibility — MEASURED, not assumed (each claim has an experiment)

* **A tools-withdrawn turn DOES emit a schema-valid verdict.** Experiment E1, `FunctionModel`
  looping unconditionally, `mode="structured"` / `output_schema="completion_verdict"`, the real
  runner: with `tool_step_limit=6` the tool surface offered per request went
  `[6, 6, 6, 6, 6, 6, 0]` and the run **returned a valid `completion_verdict`** (verdict=FAIL, one
  finding) in 7 requests. The control arm (`tool_step_limit=None`) raised `LLMRunnerError` with no
  verdict. This retires the objection recorded on ticket 9a08-614d-a9d4-4a81, whose prototype
  withdrew tools and found "the exhausted agent emitted unparseable prose": under `mode="structured"`
  the Agent is constructed with `output_type` (`structured_run.py:191-196`), so the landing turn is
  schema-constrained.
* **A runaway CAN be aborted mid-run, so it can be ROUTED rather than merely capped.** Experiment E5:
  an exception raised from inside the toolset filter predicate propagates cleanly out of
  `agent.run_sync` and survives in the `__cause__` chain (control arm, returning `False`, returns a
  verdict as in E1). **Caveat that this plan must handle:** it currently arrives at the surface as
  `LLMUnavailableError: the LLM provider call failed`, because `interpret_failure`'s third branch
  (`structured_run.py:110-155`) sweeps any unrecognised exception into the provider-outage bucket. A
  runaway misreported as a provider outage would be a NEW defect of exactly the kind this ticket
  exists to remove, so `interpret_failure` must gain a typed branch AHEAD of that fallback.
* `run_ctx.messages` and `run_ctx.usage.tool_calls` are both available inside the predicate (verified
  against `pydantic_ai.tools.RunContext` fields).
* `usage_log.failure_usage` duck-types on a plain message list (`type(m).__name__ == "ModelResponse"`
  / `"ToolCallPart"`), so the existing signature logic runs **verbatim** on the live history.

### Cost: the predicate runs ONCE PER TOOL PER STEP — the detector must not re-walk history

Measured in E5: with 6 tools registered the predicate was invoked **6 times per run step** (30 calls
across 5 steps), and the history it sees grows by 2 messages per step. Recomputing signatures over
the whole message list on every invocation is therefore O(tools x steps x history) — on a 250-request
run that is a self-inflicted cost on the healthy path this ticket promises not to disturb. The
discriminator must be computed **at most once per `run_step`** (memoised on the step number) and read
only the trailing window, never the full history.

### On runaway detection, ROUTE TO THE TOOL-FREE FINALIZER — do not land on the poisoned history

The earlier revision of this section said "withdraw tools so the agent lands a verdict on the
evidence it has". **That is superseded.** The objection that killed the flat forced landing — *a
worse verdict on degraded evidence, on a gate that SIGNS its output* — applies with equal force to
landing on a history that has just repeated one identical call 144 times (SPLIT-A). Applying that
standard consistently means the runaway's own context must not be the basis of a signed verdict.

Instead, a detected runaway routes into the **already-shipped bounded recovery + tool-free
finalizer** (`completion_recovery.py:453-521`): each explicit criterion is re-evaluated in a **fresh
history** (so the loop cannot persist), the evidence run converges after `_EVIDENCE_TOOL_STEPS=16`
(post-[rebar:e1b1-859e-a7b4-48f2] that boundary steers with synthetic tool results rather than
withdrawing tool definitions, which 400s on Bedrock/Anthropic mid-history), and a `single_turn`,
tool-free structured finalizer emits the `completion_verdict` from that clean evidence. This is the design ticket 9a08-614d-a9d4-4a81 shipped and gated on token exhaustion alone;
this ticket adds the runaway trigger it was never wired to.

Concretely the actuator becomes: detect -> raise a typed runaway error -> `interpret_failure`
classifies it (see the caveat above) -> `CompletionAgentStep.run` (`completion_recovery.py:425-431`,
which today catches only `UnretryableOutputError` under `_is_token_exhaustion`) also catches the
runaway error and calls the existing `_recover(...)`.

**Fallback if the finalizer still yields nothing.** Recovery is not assumed to succeed: it can fail
its own preconditions (`_validate_recovery_inputs`), exceed `_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS`/evidence bounds, or
the finalizer can fail validation. Every such path already raises `CompletionRecoveryError` carrying
a bounded diagnostic, and `raise_completion_workflow_failure` (`completion_recovery.py:373-402`) then
emits the `gate_error_v1` sidecar. So the terminal state is "no verdict, WITH a recorded diagnostic
naming the runaway" — strictly better than today's bare `LLMError` with `diagnostic = null`, and an
AC below pins it.

### The shared discriminator contract — THREE consumers, one definition

The signal must be pinned here, not left to "e.g. a windowed distinct-ratio", or two tickets ship
incompatible halves. The contract:

| item | value |
|---|---|
| summary field name | `distinct_ratio_window` |
| window (trailing tool calls) | `24` |
| trip condition | `distinct_ratio_window is not None and distinct_ratio_window <= 0.50` |
| semantics | set cardinality of tool-call signatures over the trailing window, divided by the window size; order-insensitive; `None` when fewer than 24 signatures exist (insufficient sample — consumers never trip on short runs) |
| producer | `usage_log._repetition_summary` (ticket 70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0) |

Consumers, all three of which must agree on that one field:
1. **this ticket's actuator**, which trips on it;
2. **[rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0]**, which produces it (its AC currently says only "*e.g.* a windowed
   distinct-ratio" and must be tightened to this exact field name, window and semantics);
3. **ticket aec1-76e7-bb95-4c86** (usage instrumentation, already claimed and in progress), which must
   record this field alongside `tool_calls` (its `_SHAPE_FIELDS` allowlist includes
   `distinct_ratio_window`) so a run's repetition profile is recoverable after the fact. (Ticket d166-036c-238c-4b39 recorded the same mechanism — the `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` no-op and the
   missing `tool_calls` field — and `aec1-76e7-bb95-4c86` is the live work ticket for it.)

The window and threshold are named constants single-sourced beside the producer, not literals buried
in the predicate.


### Both kill paths must be bound — as FAILURE conditions, not workload ceilings

`build_usage_limits` (`structured_run.py:399-412`) installs two independent ceilings:

    request_limit    = max(1, ceil(eff_max_iter / 2))   # 240 at the default max_iterations=480
    tool_calls_limit = max(8, eff_max_iter)              # 480

`run_step` increments once per **model request** (`pydantic_ai/_agent_graph.py:856`) and therefore
bounds only the first. Measured sweep: at 3 tool calls/request a `tool_step_limit` of 239, 216 **and**
180 all still die. The clean FULL run sat at 258/240 = **1.075**; ticket a89d-4dd2-f421-417a
measured a real run at 475/240 = **1.979**, clearing the 480 ceiling by **2 calls**. A guard keyed on
`run_step` alone passes a 1-call-per-request test and still dies in production.

Because the discriminator is computed over **tool calls**, a runaway that burns calls without
burning requests trips the same signal — so both paths are bound without introducing any workload
ceiling.

**Enforcement point (pinned from the vendored source):** `UsageLimits.check_before_tool_call`
(`pydantic_ai/usage.py:412-419`) is called from `_agent_graph.py:1703-1706` with **projected** usage
(`usage.tool_calls + len(calls_to_run)`) and raises **before** executing, so `usage.tool_calls` never
overshoots — the run dies instead. The guard must therefore act while headroom still remains.

---

## HONEST LIMITS OF THIS FIX — do not soften these

**1. This does NOT make e369's full-criteria close reach a verdict.** The clean FULL run never trips
the discriminator, so it would still die budget-exhausted on genuine breadth. **Per the stated design
intent that is CORRECT behaviour, not a bug to route around** — the budget bounds failures, and that
run contains no failure to bound.

**2. The path to e369 reaching a verdict is AC-split PLUS this actuator, is two tickets, and promises
no PASS.** Each half's genuine work (76 and 167 distinct calls) sits inside the budget once its loop
is cut — but "reaches a verdict" is not "passes". Criterion #1's Gerrit half remains unreachable by
any repository tool (ticket 6ec8-24c7-182b-40d0), and the flat budget still does not scale with
claim volume (ticket a89d-4dd2-f421-417a, ticket d59e-e042-2b94-4b70).

## The AC-split fallback: tested live — both halves still died; belongs in its own ticket

Split by explicit AC index (never inferred), each half carrying the full context: 14 criteria ->
7 + 7, context 99,347 -> 96,631 (A) / 96,086 (B) chars. The criteria partition cleanly (each is an
independent `- [x]` item), but **both halves still died empty**, and the per-criterion cost did not fall:

| run | criteria | distinct calls | **distinct per criterion** |
|---|---|---|---|
| FULL | 14 | 238 | 17.0 |
| SPLIT-A | 7 | 76 | 10.9 |
| SPLIT-B | 7 | 167 | **23.9** |

SPLIT-B spent **more** evidence per criterion than the full run; run-to-run variance (10.9-23.9)
dominates any halving effect. Two signatures over two disjoint criteria subsets is also a **material
change to what the attestation means** and needs its own design. It is a capability, not this bug's
fix — and only viable at all *with* this actuator, since both halves were killed by loops, not
breadth.

## Measurement gap found along the way

The control-group question ("how many requests did the epics that PASSED consume?") **could not be
answered honestly**: `usage_log.record()` no-ops unless `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` is set (unset by default),
and even then `_FIELDS` (`usage_log.py:32`) omits `tool_calls`. Filed as
ticket d166-036c-238c-4b39 — a gate whose spend cannot be measured after the fact cannot be tuned,
the same "computed then discarded" shape as ticket 8b97-a0ca-82a4-4d4e.
